name: Death and Graves
description: GraveStone keeps everything you carried in a grave where you died.

pages.title: Death and Graves
pages.text:
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Key points**

- Dying leaves a **grave** with everything you carried.
- Break the grave to get it all back, armour and Curios slots included.
- The Latest Death waypoint on your map leads you back.
- Anyone can break it, so a friend can fetch it.

pages.title: Gravestone
pages.text: When you die, **GraveStone** puts a grave where you fell and stores your inventory, armour, offhand and Curios slots (backpack, charms) in it. Nothing drops on the ground, so nothing burns or despawns.

Walk back and break the grave: every item goes back where it was. Aether gloves and pendants come back as normal items; put them on again with **comma**.\
\
You also get an **Obituary**, a paper saying how and where you died. It disappears when you break the grave.

**Where graves land:**

- **Void** (falling out of the world, as in the End): just above the bottom of the world, in the rock. Dig down to it.
- **Lava**: in the lava where you died. Bring Fire Resistance or drain it first.
- **Water**: on the spot, even deep underwater.

- **On a ship**: in the air where you died. The ship flies on and the grave stays there, so follow the Latest Death waypoint and build up to it.
- **Another planet**: on that planet, where you died. You wake up back on Earth, so you need a rocket to fetch it.

[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Tip:** an **Everlasting Upgrade** keeps a backpack safe from fire, lava and the void if it ever lies on the ground, for example after you drop it. See [#](2E5AAC)[Backpacks and Storage](entry://home/storage)[#]().\
\
The server also keeps regular backups of the world; see [#](2E5AAC)[Playing Together](entry://start_here/playing_together)[#]().
